title: Choose the notification channel from the plug-ins that shipped

blocks.text: The notification service sends alerts to operators through one of several channels: SMS, email, push. Each channel ships as a jar of its own, so a customer installs only the channels they pay for, and the service never names a channel class in its code. A channel's jar holds a class that implements `Channels.Notifier`, carries `@Channels.Channel("<name>")`, and is listed in that jar's `META-INF/services/practice.Channels$Notifier`. The service's configuration names the channel to use.

The service keeps its plug-in jars in a class loader of their own and hands it to `Channels.forChannel(channel, plugins)`, the method you write in `src/main/java/practice/Channels.java`. Last week's incidents decide what it must do:

items: the service started on a thread whose context class loader can't see the plug-in jars, and it found no channel at all;
a customer installed the push jar without its key; push's constructor throws, and the SMS alerts they had configured stopped too;
a typo in the configuration (`"emial"`) sent the alerts somewhere other than where the customer asked, and nobody noticed for a week.

blocks.text: Return the configured channel's notifier, built once. A channel that no plug-in provides fails with `IllegalArgumentException`, and its message names the channel. About seven lines.

cases.says: the configured channel's notifier is returned and delivers through that channel
channels are found through the class loader passed in, even when the calling thread's context class loader can't see them
a channel whose constructor fails, listed before the configured one, does not stop the configured one from being found
only the configured channel's notifier is constructed; the other channels are never started
a channel no plug-in provides is refused with IllegalArgumentException naming it, not answered with another channel

origin.section: Iterating the Loader Builds Every Provider Before the One You Want

concepts: Iterating a ServiceLoader constructs each provider it passes, so one that can't start fails the lookup; stream() with Provider.type() chooses without constructing, and load(type, loader) looks where it is told instead of the context class loader.
